title: Cutting your cloud bill is easy. Cutting it while improving performance is the actual job.
excerpt: A migration is a single event. Optimisation is a discipline. What the best cloud programmes do differently — and why most leave value on the table.
author: Algorims Cloud Practice

body.text: A migration is a single event. Optimisation is a discipline. The organisations that get the most out of the cloud are the ones who treat the post-migration phase as the real beginning of the work — not the end of a project.

items: Portfolio rationalisation first. Decommission what shouldn't have been migrated in the first place. Most estates have 10–20% of workloads that quietly cost more than they're worth.
Right-size before you move. The cloud is elastic, but only if you ask it to be. Defaulted instance sizes are how organisations pay 3× for capacity they don't use.
Pick the right 'R'. Rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retire. The mix matters far more than the headline 'we moved to cloud'.
Build the FinOps muscle on day one. Tagging, allocation, showback — not a Q4 panic when the bill arrives.

body.text: Reserved instances and savings plans are the obvious lever — and most organisations leave a third of the available discount on the table. The less obvious wins are architectural: managed services instead of self-run databases, serverless where workloads are spiky, storage tiering, and ruthless attention to data egress.
Hybrid is not a dirty word

For regulated workloads, latency-sensitive operations, or specific data residency requirements, hybrid is still the right answer. The mistake is treating hybrid as a permanent state of indecision rather than a deliberate architecture.

Workload assessment, migration design, FinOps installation, and the unglamorous but high-value work of continuous optimisation. Most of our clients see the bill come down within a quarter — and performance improve at the same time.
